newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil ignores crude rally, sour barges fall.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil ignores crude rally, sour barges fall.

text.p: NWE fuel oil all but ignored crude's rally on Tuesday, traders said.

Low sulphur cracked cargoes were the subject of some disagreement, with some traders evaluating the grade at an unchanged $128 fob and others pointing to a prompt cargo looking for bids at $125 fob Scandinavia.

The cargo on offer from Gothenburg was fixed on a 50,000 tonnes vessel to sail to the Mediterranean, shipping brokers said. A December-loading cargo was available from Rotterdam at a swaps-related price.
Italy received low sulphur cargo offers below $138 cif Milazzo, which nets back to around $125 fob NWE.
Many dealers thought that low sulphur's recent rise from $121 to $128 fob NWE was a speculative bubble which was now deflating.
A high sulphur cracked cargo from Coryton was sold at $114.50 cif Swansea, steady on Monday's level, but barges fell by up to $5 at one point in the day, ending $3 lower at $110 fob ARA.
Utility demand was steady, but some dealers expected prices to pick up as winter demand kicked in.
